turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hey there, how have things been?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm about to buy a tent and I keep going back and forth between three of them.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll describe them all, so please hold off until I'm done.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a big cabin-style tent for six, tall enough to stand up in, but it weighs almost thirty pounds.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Another is a light two-person backpacking tent, barely four pounds, though it's snug once the gear is inside.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then there's a pop-up tent that sets itself up in seconds and it's cheap, but reviews say it struggles in wind.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It really depends on how you camp. If you drive right to your pitch, the cabin tent's comfort is hard to beat, but the backpacking one is the only sensible pick if you'll carry it. I'd be wary of the pop-up if your sites get windy.
